clue.text: Repeat sound set elsewhere...

indicators.note: sound tells the solver to say a phrase out loud and keep what the ear hears, not the spelling

blocks.note: to re-site something is to set it in another place

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to repeat a sound effect that was recorded on a different set.
explanation.walkthrough: RESITE and RECITE are said the same way. The ellipsis runs on into the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to say aloud from memory, which is a way of repeating words already learnt.

clue.text: Engineer cryptic clues one doesn't want to be seen

definitions.text: one doesn't want to be seen

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling and obscure, hinting that the letters are disguised in a scrambled order

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A crossword setter devises clues so cryptic that the solver can make nothing of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse is a hermit who shuns company, someone who avoids being seen by others.

clue.text: He wears a hat, which is reasonable

indicators.note: a hat that is worn sits around the head, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A man puts on a hat whose price is fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wears' reads as a man donning a hat, but it means one word sits inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap and reasonable both describe a price that is low and affordable rather than expensive.

clue.text: Model priest - false prophet, of course

indicators.note: something false is not genuine, so these letters are not in their true order

blocks.note: the Model T was Henry Ford's famous car
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An exemplary clergyman turns out to be a false prophet, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like a casual aside but means of the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster forecasts the winners of horse races, so he is a predictor at the racecourse.

clue.text: ...  in Greece, or some in South Africa

definitions.note: the clue gives the place by its location; the answer is a city in Greece

indicators.note: in places the word for some inside the letters standing for the country

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for South Africa
some of something is a part of it

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: a sound set somewhere in Greece, or else somewhere in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is S(PART)A. The opening ellipsis links the surface to 1 across, as though the set were in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was the famous militaristic city-state of ancient Greece in the Peloponnese, and a modern town stands there today.

clue.text: Vigorous frolic in jerks to strict time

definitions.note: a phrase meaning on time, standing for the adjective

indicators.note: in puts the word for the frolic inside the letters for the exercises

blocks.note: physical jerks is British slang for keep-fit exercises, known as PT, physical training
a romp is lively, boisterous play

explanation.surface: Energetic play carried out in sudden movements, all strictly in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerks' looks like sudden movements, but physical jerks are gym exercises, a British term.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt means punctual, done exactly at the appointed moment without any delay.

clue.text: Strangely under and over time, which is superfluous

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters are arranged oddly
in a down entry, one piece written over another comes above it, so it goes first

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Time spent both under and over, oddly, turns out to be more than needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something redundant is surplus to requirements, exactly what superfluous describes.

clue.text: Currently a scholar at Magdalen, or other place of learning

definitions.note: Magdalen is a college, so the answer is another such place

blocks.note: AC is alternating current, an electric current
taken as written
at Magdalen College, Oxford, a scholar holding a foundation award is called a demy

explanation.surface: Someone is presently studying at Magdalen College or some other seat of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Currently' reads as 'at present' but signals electrical current. The demy is a peculiarity of Magdalen.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school or college, an institution where people go to be taught.

clue.text: Dig up frisky steed without prejudice

indicators.note: a frisky animal jumps about, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: to disinter is to exhume from the ground
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to unearth a lively horse, impartially.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinterested means impartial, having no personal stake that could bias one's judgment.

clue.text: Unrestricted use of cane may cause skin inflammation

indicators.note: used without restriction, the letters are free to go in any order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that caning pupils without limit may leave their skin inflamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a condition of inflamed pores and spots on the skin, common in teenagers.

clue.text: Stiffly formal, or laid back from the start

indicators.note: back means the word for put down is read from its end to its beginning

blocks.note: prim means stiffly proper
taken as written
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: Someone is either stiff and formal or relaxed, right from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid back' looks like the idiom for relaxed, but the two words split into fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Primordial means existing at or since the very beginning of time, original and primeval.

clue.text: Place for the preacher - and what he can do with his sermon!

definitions.text: what he can do with his sermon
definitions.note: a verb phrase, read as two words

blocks.note: first meaning: the raised stand in a church from which sermons are given

blocks.clueFragment: what he can do with his sermon
blocks.note: second meaning, split into two words: he can mash it up and throw it away

explanation.surface: A dig at a preacher: here is where he stands, and here is what to do with his sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as PULP IT, the second reading tells the preacher to destroy his own sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulpit is the enclosed platform in a church where the preacher stands; to pulp paper is to pulverise it.

clue.text: Threatened to have done with the devil

indicators.note: with means placed alongside, joining two words end to end

blocks.note: an imp is a little devil
to have done is to have finished

explanation.surface: Someone threatened to be finished with the devil once and for all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that impended was hanging over people, looming as a menace about to happen.

clue.text: Like Dan Dare, steep tumble down

indicators.note: things that tumble down fall in a jumble, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: both words taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Dan Dare, the comic-book space hero, takes a tumble down a steep slope.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Dare is a British comic hero, but the Dan wanted is Desperate Dan, the cowboy of the Dandy comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate Dan is the brawny cowboy of the British children's comic the Dandy, so being like him is being desperate.

clue.text: A number in Kent town find parking turns on a magic device

indicators.note: in puts the number inside the name of the Kent town
find here adds the next piece on, as though it were found at the end
turns means the whole string is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Margate is a seaside resort in Kent
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A number in a Kent town finds parking spaces depend on a magic charm.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside MARGATE before its last letter, P follows, and the whole is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagram is a five-pointed star drawn as a symbol in magic and the occult.

clue.text: This has cut smoking

blocks.note: surface reading: something has reduced how much people smoke
setter's reading: the word goes with cut to name a tobacco for smoking

explanation.walkthrough: Navy Cut is a well-known brand of pipe tobacco and cigarettes, so this word plus cut gives something to smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleet's name forms the first half of Navy Cut, a pressed tobacco originally sold to sailors.

clue.text: Habit won't let one drop the apostrophe

indicators.note: dropping the apostrophe removes the punctuation mark and leaves only the letters

blocks.note: the contraction with its punctuation taken out

explanation.surface: A refusal to let a habitual apostrophe be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A wont is a custom or habitual practice, as in 'as is my wont'.

clue.text: Cautionary cry in Somerset

definitions.note: the answer is a place found in that county, given by location

blocks.note: a warning to be careful, as a West Country voice might say it

explanation.surface: A West Country warning shout to look out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Somerset' does two jobs: it locates the town and tells the solver to hear the warning in a local accent. Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Watchet is a small harbour town on the Bristol Channel coast of Somerset, in south-west England.

clue.text: The chief has Jag - early model

blocks.note: arch means chief, as in archenemy
the E-type is a classic Jaguar sports car, Jag for short

explanation.surface: The boss owns a Jaguar, an early version of the car.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the original pattern from which copies are made, the first prototype.

clue.text: Dogged?

blocks.note: surface reading: an adjective meaning stubbornly persistent
setter's reading: a verb meaning followed relentlessly, as a pack of dogs would

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark asks the solver to take the word as a verb about being chased by dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pursued persistently is to be harried, as a hunting pack chases its quarry.

clue.text: Religious teaching many found in head (of Church)

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside, so these pieces go within the word for head

blocks.note: pate is an old word for the head
RI is religious instruction, a school subject
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Religious instruction for many people is located in the leader of the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' does double duty: it is the outer piece of the wordplay and, with the bracketed words, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A primate is an archbishop, the senior bishop of a province or country such as England.

clue.text: Upset tables are not easily upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, leaving the letters in disarray

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An observation that tables, even knocked over, are hard to topple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' appears twice: first as the signal to rearrange, then inside the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is steady and firmly balanced, unlikely to tip or be disturbed.

clue.text: Sat Latin translation in a lost realm of fancy

indicators.note: a translation renders words into a different form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: both words taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil sat a Latin translation exam about a legendary vanished kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the mythical island civilisation, described by Plato, said to have sunk beneath the sea.

clue.text: Old city feature may be seen in the gutter

definitions.text: may be seen in the gutter
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a street child, not a direct synonym

blocks.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
the chin is one of the facial features

explanation.surface: An architectural feature of an ancient city now lies in a roadside gutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' suggests a building but means part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is a poor, ragged child of the streets, a guttersnipe found playing in the road.

clue.text: Dog chewed cigar, having got nothing for one

indicators.note: having got one thing for another means a swap, putting the new letter in place of the old
something chewed is mangled, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
O looks like zero
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A dog gnawed a cigar and was left with nothing for its trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed of dog, famously kept by the Queen.

clue.text: Brea

blocks.note: surface reading: a meaningless string, or a place name
setter's reading: a five-letter word for a baked loaf, missing its last letter, so a curtailed version of it

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a visual pun: a word for a loaf with its final letter cut off is literally that loaf made short, which names a Scottish biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortbread is a crumbly butter biscuit from Scotland, and the clue shows bread literally shortened.

clue.text: The way to take in the broadest spectrum

indicators.note: to take in is to contain, so the letters sit inside the next word

blocks.note: four letters inside the word
surface padding: it completes the phrase broad spectrum and gives no letters

explanation.surface: Advice on the best way to absorb the widest range of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a route from one place to another, a way to travel along.

clue.text: Doctor in row over possible deal

indicators.note: in places the doctor inside the word for a row

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor is having an argument about a potential business agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel and 'deal' as an agreement, but deal is pine wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is sawn pine or fir board, so it is one possible kind of wood for building.

clue.text: A dunderhead in place of intelligence

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the word splits into dunder plus its own signal, keeping the opening letter
vice is Latin for in place of, as in vice-president

explanation.surface: An idiot is sitting where clever thinking ought to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dunderhead' splits into dunder plus the signal for its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence in its old sense means news or information, and advice once meant a report or tidings.
